page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-180-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-intensive server instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 180 dedicated virtual CPUs (90 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled) and 1440.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a massive local storage array consisting of 16 NVMe SSDs totaling 6432 GB of high-speed local storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is exceptionally strong, with read-only small block cached bandwidth and large block write bandwidth both ranking in the top 10%. The server also excels in specialized compute tasks, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. For database and memory-bound workloads, the instance delivers top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, processing 212.07 million operations per second, alongside strong database operations in Passmark testing. Large-scale language model (LLM) inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds across small, medium, and large models, despite the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

Given its massive memory capacity, high-density local NVMe storage, and top-tier multi-core compute capabilities, the c3d-highmem-180-lssd offers high resource density. This makes it a highly cost-efficient platform for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads without requiring the overhead of dedicated GPU accelerators. The instance is optimized for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, high-throughput data processing pipelines, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
